base.intentNote: Base phase rewards movement quality and capacity build. Allow exercise variation week-to-week to expose the athlete to a broad pattern repertoire.

build.intentNote: Build phase locks exercise selection so progression signal is interpretable. Vary load/reps/tempo, not exercise identity.

peak.intentNote: Peak phase keeps the exact compound stack from build and pushes intensity. New exercises are explicitly disallowed.

taper.intentNote: Taper preserves stimulus signature while reducing fatigue. Keep exercises and intensity, drop volume.

race.intentNote: Race week is dress rehearsal only. No new stimulus.

deload.intentNote: Deload allows movement variety at low load. Use it to address weak patterns without accumulating fatigue.

maintenance.intentNote: Maintenance phase keeps tissue resilience. Bias toward minimum effective dose. Variety is a bonus, not a requirement.

novice.intentNote: Novices need few patterns repeated frequently to learn. Cap session breadth and skip advanced/expert lifts until form is grooved.

intermediate.intentNote: Intermediates can handle full pattern surface. Tempo and pause variants become available as progression knobs.

advanced.intentNote: Advanced athletes can use the full catalog including expert-tier lifts and complex tempo schemes.

bodyweight_only.intentNote: Bodyweight athletes progress via tempo and leverage manipulation, not load. Reps are the last knob to turn.

bodyweight_plus_bar.intentNote: Pull-up bar unlocks vertical pulling progressions. Otherwise treat like bodyweight_only.

dumbbells_only.intentNote: Dumbbells favor unilateral and stable bilateral work. Skip max-strength low-rep schemes; lean into hypertrophy ranges.

full_gym.intentNote: Full gym unlocks the entire compound stack. Progression should run on linear or undulating load schemes.

progressionRules.rationale: If the athlete completes target reps at sub-RPE 8 for two consecutive sessions, the lift is ready for a 2.5% load bump.
For accessory work, add a rep when the top set still leaves 2+ reps in reserve.
Bodyweight lifts can't grow load-wise. When reps top out, increase eccentric tempo by 1s to extend time-under-tension.
When eccentric tempo hits 5s and reps are still hit, the next progression level (harder leverage variant) is unlocked.
If a key session was missed, do not progress volume that week. Re-baseline before pushing again.
Persistent high soreness or moderate pain drops load 10% next session, preserving the movement pattern.
Yellow/red readiness suppresses threshold and VO2 work for the day. Aerobic base preserves fitness without piling on stress.

interferenceRules.intentNote: Six hours between heavy strength and key endurance protects the higher-priority discipline. If schedule forces same-day, key endurance comes first.

sessionRoleRotation.intentNote: Roles must not repeat within a week. Lower/upper alternation is preserved when sessions ≥ 4 days. For three-day weeks, prefer full-body density days to avoid leaving any pattern undertrained.

sessionStructure.intentNote: A calisthenics session opens with the highest-skill movement (handstand work, lever, weighted bodyweight strength) when CNS is fresh, then runs antagonist supersets, then a core/density finisher.

progressionPath.intentNote: Each path is ordered by progression difficulty. The engine advances along the path when the athlete completes target reps with target tempo for two consecutive sessions.

tempoProgressionScheme.intentNote: Tempo digits = eccentric / bottom pause / concentric / top pause in seconds. The intermediate scheme is the workhorse for hypertrophy. Advanced (5s eccentric) is the gating tempo before unlocking the next leverage variant.
